ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, headings, icon strokes, hairline borders, deep surfaces — the near-black backbone that makes white space read as gallery rather than form

paper.$description: Paper — Primary canvas and card surface — the default ground for the entire directory

mist.$description: Mist — Secondary surface for subtle bands, input fills, and tag/chip backgrounds that need to sit just behind Paper

hairline.$description: Hairline — Borders, dividers, and outlined-button strokes — the thinnest visible structural line

slate.$description: Slate — Secondary body text and muted nav labels — never used as a primary heading color

fog.$description: Fog — Tertiary text, placeholder text, disabled labels

graphite.$description: Graphite — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI.

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Primary filled button background, elevated card surface, and tag pill fill — the single non-neutral action color

deep-ink.$description: Deep Ink — Heaviest text weight and maximum-contrast border accents on dark cards

pearl.$description: Pearl — Icon strokes on white surfaces and faint structural outlines

iris.$description: Iris — Category/challenge card background — vivid violet used as one of the rotating card-fill colors

lilac.$description: Lilac — Soft violet wash for decorative surfaces and pale category cards

orchid.$description: Orchid — Vivid pink-purple card fill in the category carousel

wine.$description: Wine — Deep muted plum card fill in the category carousel

coral.$description: Coral — Warm red card fill in the category carousel and highlight badges

lime.$description: Lime — Vivid green-yellow card fill and decorative wash — the brightest accent in the palette

hero-wash.$description: Hero Wash — Hero background gradient running from icy cyan through sky blue into soft violet — the only multi-color wash on the page

gt-standard-m.$description: Workhorse for body text, navigation, buttons, labels, input fields, and most headings up to 24px. The 15–16px body with tight -0.01em tracking and generous 1.50 line-height is what gives Contra its editorial-density feel without sacrificing legibility.

gt-standard-l.$description: Reserved for the largest display moments (the 58px hero headline) and small uppercase eyebrows (8px at 0.15em tracking). The 0.88–1.05 line-heights at display sizes let the headline 'Get more creative' sit on a single tight block — a magazine-cover move, not a UI move.
